notes: **Definition**: if $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors, their scalar product (dot product) is $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between them. The result is a scalar, e.g. $c=\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos\theta$.
**Case 1 â€” perpendicular vectors**: if $\theta=90Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos90Â°=0$. This is the condition for two vectors to be perpendicular.
**Case 2 â€” parallel vectors**: if $\theta=0Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos0Â°=ab$. This is the condition for two vectors to be parallel.
**Case 3 â€” anti-parallel vectors**: if $\theta=180Â°$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos180Â°=-ab$. This is the condition for two vectors to be anti-parallel.

**Dot products of unit vectors**: since the angle between a unit vector and itself is 0Â°: $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{i}=\hat{j}\cdot\hat{j}=\hat{k}\cdot\hat{k}=1$. Since $\hat{i},\hat{j},\hat{k}$ are mutually perpendicular (90Â°): $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{j}=\hat{j}\cdot\hat{k}=\hat{k}\cdot\hat{i}=0$.

**Component-form derivation**: for $\vec{A}=A_1\hat{i}+A_2\hat{j}+A_3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B}=B_1\hat{i}+B_2\hat{j}+B_3\hat{k}$, expanding $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}$ term by term and using the unit-vector dot products above gives $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}=A_1B_1+A_2B_2+A_3B_3$.
